user.title: Configure Home Mind
user.description: Enter the URL of your Home Mind API server. Don't have a server? Get a hosted one at [{cloud_url}]({cloud_url}).

data_description.api_token: Required for Home Mind Cloud. Leave empty for self-hosted setups without authentication.
data_description.user_id: Namespaces memory per person. Used when a request carries no Home Assistant user context — e.g. a voice satellite.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the Home Mind API. Make sure it's running and accessible.
error.invalid_auth: Invalid API token. Check your token on the Home Mind Cloud dashboard.

init.title: Home Mind — model & options
init.description: Choose the AI provider and set the options. Model and API key come in the next step.

data.prefer_local: Try simple commands locally first (free, 0 tokens)
data.web_search_mode: How the assistant searches the web

data_description.prefer_local: Simple commands ("turn on the living room light", "what time is it") are answered by Home Assistant's built-in agent — locally, nothing leaves the house, no cost. Only what HA does not recognise is passed to the AI.
data_description.web_search_limit: Every search is another full LLM round-trip carrying the whole prompt, which makes it the most expensive tool. 0 = internet off (the agent says so instead of guessing), 1 = frugal (recommended), higher = more thorough but pricier.
data_description.memory_token_limit: Token budget for facts about you and your home, recalled from the memory store and attached to EVERY request. More memory = the assistant knows you better and asks less, but each request costs more and is slower. 1500 is roughly 50-60 facts. 0 = no memory: the assistant knows nothing from earlier conversations and the server skips the memory lookup entirely (cheapest).
data_description.custom_prompt: Replaces the default personality line. Leave empty to keep the default.
data_description.web_search_mode: grounding — the model searches inside its own request: one API call, cheapest and fastest, but it needs a Google project WITH billing (the free tier rejects it). gemini_micro — search runs as a small separate request on a second, billed key, so the conversation itself can stay on a free key; costs one extra round-trip. searxng — a metasearch instance running on your own server: no key, no account and nothing to run out of, though the public engines behind it can rate-limit your connection. tavily / brave — a third-party search API; Google sees nothing, but you get raw snippets instead of a written answer. Whichever you pick, the server tracks what is left on each backend and moves to another one that still has free allowance; when none does, it stops searching rather than spending money.

data.search_api_key: Search API key (billed Google project, optional)

data_description.api_key: Leave blank to keep the key already stored on the server. Paste a new one to switch to another Google project (e.g. a free-tier one) or to rotate the key. The key is stored by the Home Mind server, not by Home Assistant.
data_description.model: For Ollama the list shows what is installed on the machine, with the VRAM each model needs. Entries marked DO POBRANIA are not downloaded yet — pull one first (`docker exec home-mind-ollama ollama pull <model>`), otherwise the first request fails. A model larger than the card still runs: Ollama moves the rest to system RAM and it becomes several times slower.
data_description.base_url: For the OpenAI-compatible provider, and for Ollama when it runs on another machine (default: the Ollama container next to the server). Keep the suggested value unless you know you need a different endpoint.
data_description.search_api_key: Only needed for the gemini_micro search mode. Key of a Google project WITH billing — it pays for search only (5000 grounded queries/month are included), while the conversation keeps running on the key above. Leave blank to keep the stored one.
data_description.thinking: Lets the model reason before answering. Turn it OFF if the assistant goes silent or takes tens of seconds: a reasoning model can spend its ENTIRE output budget on an internal monologue and return nothing at all. Ollama only - hosted providers reject the setting.
